pr_title: Optimize api calls between envoy_reader and Home Assistant
pr_body:
<!--

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
The current sensor code makes one API call for each inverter installed in the Enphase solar system. For Enphase systems the solar panel and inverter have a 1-to-1 relationship. Most systems have at least 8 solar panels.  I have seen some systems with 32 and in extreme cases 300+. These multiple calls for inverter data is actually repetitive because the page containing the data is all or nothing. As well some older Envoy devices can become unresponsive and not return data when too many requests are sent to it.

So this change on the Home Assistant sensor side is to make one http call for all of the inverters and display the individual inverter data in Home Assistant using the coordinator

[envoy_reader changelog@0.17.3...0.18.2](https://github.com/jesserizzo/envoy_reader/compare/0.17.3...0.18.2)
Changes to the `envoy_reader` library include:
- Remove `update()` method that Home Assistant previously used
- Change to raising exceptions when errors occur
- Replaced `requests_async` library with `httpx`
- Move all I/O operations to a single function `getData()`
- Automatic retry when gathering Inverter data. Moving to `httpx` seems to uncovered an underlying issue with older Envoy devices

**Last working Home Assistant release (if known):** N/A - Hasn't worked since at least .98 when I first started getting things running


**Operating environment (Hass.io/Docker/Windows/etc.):**  hass.io running inside an Ubuntu VM on a large multi-Xeon vmWare server

**Integration:** https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/enphase_envoy/

**Description of problem:**  I have an Enphase Envoy solar system, controlled by an "S" model controller.  While summary production numbers are being produced, individual inverter statistics are stuck as "Unknown".  My Home Assistant logs are filling up with two relevant errors:

```
2020-01-02 18:57:33 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.helpers.entity] Update for sensor.envoy_solar_controllerenvoy_inverter_121731044406 fails
```

review_comments: If you would inherit from `CoordinatorEntity` then the update process should become a bit easier. The data would automatically be passed down from the coordinator.
Inherited CoordinatorEntity, is this all I have to do?

There is a bit more:
* No need to override `should_poll`.
* No need to override `available`.
* No need to override `async_added_to_hass`.
* And you want to transform the code from `async_update` into overriding `state`. (There is a high-level introduction into `CoordinatorEntity` at https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/integration_fetching_data/)
Oh, and you only need to inherit from `CoordinatorEntity`, not from `Entity` anymore.

Sorry put the comment in the wrong section! 😮 

- Removed should_poll
- Removed available
- Removed async_added_to_hass
- Removed async_update and moved the code into state
- In state it wasn't a copy and paste from async_update, but mostly the same code exists. Tried to reduce the paths and catch the same errors. I moved the update for the inverter last_reported attribute into the device_state_attributes() method

I noticed now the sensors have values on the first poll rather than waiting for the second poll!
Does this call not do I/O?
